scope: AI-008 user-managed ImportantMatter contracts, encrypted owner-scoped CRUD/CAS, independent purpose grants, deterministic expiry, MEM-002 Safety, MATTER deletion guard/cleanup, and MEM-001/MEM-002 client flows

assertions: Matter title is NFC, single-line, 1..80 graphemes and at most 320 UTF-8 bytes while owner/internal fields are rejected
create, update, transition and explicit deletion commands are strict, CAS-bound and reject ambiguous date patches
MatterView and MatterListView expose only title, date, status, independent Daily/Weekly grant booleans, revision and update time
dated matters remain ACTIVE through the target date and expire on the next product date
undated matters remain ACTIVE for seven product dates and become EXPIRED on day eight
PAUSED, COMPLETED and EXPIRED remain distinct while reactivation is explicit and cannot reuse a past target date
MEM-002 Safety runs before encrypted owner-scoped Matter persistence
PROFESSIONAL_BOUNDARY saves a private source with both ordinary AI grants closed
HIGH_RISK activates the fixed Safety overlay and ordinary Matter persistence remains zero
indeterminate Safety fails closed and CAS conflicts return only the latest MatterView
real Nest HTTP creates, lists, updates, pauses, resumes and starts one explicit MATTER DataTask
strict request parsing rejects owner injection, newline/overlong titles and same command refs with changed payloads
Matter responses contain no account, ciphertext, key version, grant ref or fingerprint
HIGH_RISK returns SafetyView and calls the ordinary Matter store zero times
malformed and over-budget Matter titles are rejected before ordinary persistence
high-risk Matter title handling returns only fixed Safety projection without echoing the title
successful deletion removes the Matter from the next management list without exposing a reverse clue

T-AI008-DB-001.selector: AI-008 real PostgreSQL Matter encryption, grants, CAS, expiry, Safety and deletion guard
assertions: PostgreSQL 18 stores only ciphertext/key version, isolates owners and keeps Daily and Weekly grants independent
same command replay converges, changed payload conflicts and two concurrent revision-one updates produce one winner
undated day-eight expiry advances revision and sets EXPIRED while an invalid dated resume leaves no command receipt
MEM-002 Safety state blocks ordinary create and repeated activation produces one decision/state
MATTER DataTask guard immediately excludes the source from list/get before restricted physical cleanup

T-AI008-DB-AI-EVAL-001.selector: AI-008 real PostgreSQL Matter encryption, grants, CAS, expiry, Safety and deletion guard
assertions: owner, purpose, revision, expiry and Safety inputs deterministically converge without reading or persisting plaintext
a deletion guard wins over subsequent Matter reads and no deleted title can be recovered through the management projection

T-AI008-DELETE-DB-001.selector: C-014 PG18 TX-09, restricted cleanup, receipt and account destruction
assertions: restricted MATTER cleanup removes the exact source, revisions, grants, dependency and encrypted personalized fragment
a published slot with a prevalidated fallback remains AVAILABLE without the deleted personalized fragment or model call

T-AI008-DELETE-AI-EVAL-001.selector: C-014 PG18 TX-09, restricted cleanup, receipt and account destruction
assertions: MATTER deletion switches to the already validated no-source fallback and removes every active title-bearing dependency
the deletion path does not call a provider, regenerate history or recover content from a receipt
Matter drafts are normalized in memory and never written to local storage
transient retry reuses one command ref while revision conflict replaces the draft baseline with the latest server projection
Safety clears the pending ordinary write and exposes only the Safety route
Mini Program list/create/update/transition/delete paths use authenticated idempotent request allowlists
client response projection rejects ciphertext, key version and unknown restricted fields
AES-256-GCM uses random IVs and rejects ciphertext or key-version tampering
the keyed title fingerprint is stable for idempotency without storing plaintext or an ordinary reversible hash
